text:
maria.d: Heads-up — scheduling a short maintenance window tomorrow 03:00-03:45 UTC to run a coordinated KV cache pruning job + a critical kernel security patch on a subset of serving nodes. Expected customer-visible effect: brief latency spikes and transient 503s for <1% of requests while affected nodes drain. Will post status page and customer note.

ton y.r: @maria.d can we keep the EU regions staggered? last time we saw traffic blips when both regions drained at once.

maria.d: yes — plan is staggered by 15m: us-west1 (03:00), eu-west1 (03:15), ap-southeast1 (03:30). each region has ~15m drain + 15m patch + 15m validation. total per-region impact window ~30m.

oncall-bot: Paging rule check: Region owners on-call will be paged for >5% error-rate or >200ms p50 increase sustained for 5m. Pager escalation: on-call -> devops-lead -> eng-sre.

sarah_ops: Draft status-page blurb below — feel free to tweak before I publish: 

"Scheduled maintenance: Targeted KV cache pruning and security patching"
"Start: 2025-04-03 03:00 UTC (staggered regions)"
"Estimated duration: up to 45 minutes per region"
"Impact: You may see short, intermittent latency increases or transient failures (estimated <1% of requests). No data will be lost. If you rely on Dedicated clusters, failover to warm pools will be used where configured."

maria.d: +1 to that blurb. Add: "We will update here and on the status page at start/completion and if rollback is required."

customer-ops: Draft customer email (short):
"We’re planning a brief maintenance window to improve system reliability. During this time some requests may experience transient errors or latency. No data loss expected. If you rely on strict SLAs, please reach out and we can coordinate a dedicated maintenance slot."

devops-lead: Ops play (condensed):
1) Pre-checks at T-60m: confirm drain scripts, KV prune dry-run, backups healthy.
2) T-15m: open maintenance incident in #incidents with incident-bot and post status page draft.
3) T0: start draining, monitor p50/p95 and 5m error rate.
4) If >5% errors or any customer-facing 5xx spikes, abort patch on remaining nodes and rollback to pre-patch kernel.
5) Post-checks: run canary inference, run integration smoke test, close incident with timeline.

oncall-bot: Incident created: incident-37328. Auto-assign -> current on-call: tony.r.

tony.r: I’ll take the pager. quick q — what’s the rollback command for the kernel package?

devops-lead: rollback is: `sudo apt-get install --allow-downgrades kernel-image-5.15.0-rt-rollback` then `systemctl reboot --no-block`. also we have image snapshots for immediate redeploy if node fails to recover.

sarah_ops: Can someone add a short FAQ line for customers: "Will this affect API keys/ tokens?" Answer: "No, auth tokens are unaffected."

maria.d: Added to the blurb. Final status page text ready to publish at T-15.

oncall-bot: Reminder scheduled: Post status page update at 2025-04-03 02:45 UTC and again at maintenance start and completion.

customer-ops: Suggestion: add opt-out contact line for high-SLA customers to request a custom window.

maria.d: Good call — added contact link: support@redwood-inference.com with subject line "Maintenance opt-out / custom window".

ton y.r: One more: add a query to watch for during rolling drain: `sum(rate(http_requests_total{status=~"5.."}[5m])) by (region)` — if it spikes > threshold, we abort.

devops-lead: noted. I’ll add dashboard panel and an alert.

maria.d: Publishing status page in 5. publishing now. :rocket: 

oncall-bot: Status page updated: https://status.redwood.ai/incident/nu-20250403-kv-kernel-maint

customer-ops: Sending customer advisory (segmented: Dedicated customers + those with recent high traffic) — queued.

ton y.r: I’m standing by on the pager. ping me if alerts fire.

maria.d: Thanks everyone. Post-maint checklist assigned to @devops-lead and @sarah_ops for verification and close-out notes. Will post completion message here when all regions report healthy. :white_check_mark:
